title: More Weather Changes For The AI Supply Chain
gist: Gavekal says the AI investment environment is shifting after the US midterms and the scandal around Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, affecting permitting, export controls and financing. The US Commerce Department tightened chip export controls, while the government prepares a list of 'national champions' to receive expedited export licenses. (Teaser only; the four developments are paywalled.)

insights.claim: The US Commerce Department announced tighter export controls on US chips on Monday 16 November 2026, as scrutiny intensified on loopholes Chinese companies used to gain direct or indirect access to Nvidia's advanced AI chips.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tighter controls hit Nvidia's China-linked revenue and intermediaries; watch for channel-checking enforcement.
insights.quote: the US Commerce Department announced tighter export controls on US chips Monday

insights.claim: The US government is preparing a list of 'national champions' that will receive expedited export licenses for AI chips.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Favored firms gain a licensing moat; selection of champions could re-rate winners vs. excluded peers.
insights.quote: the US government is preparing a list of “national champions” that will receive expedited export licenses

themes.theme: Political shocks reshaping AI supply chain

insights.claim: Gavekal argues the US midterm elections and the romantic affairs of Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang are already affecting domestic permitting, export controls and financing for AI investment.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: AI capex assumptions (permits, financing, export access) now carry elevated political risk premia.
insights.quote: These two developments are already starting to affect domestic permitting, export controls and financing.
